message.content:
Sure! A quick way to get a ball‑park figure is to look at the **average electricity use per square foot** for homes in your region. In the United States, the average residential household consumes roughly **5–6 kWh per square foot per year** (though this can vary widely depending on climate, insulation, appliances, and lifestyle).

### Rough Estimate for a 2,000 sq ft Home

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| **Annual consumption** | ≈ 10,000 kWh/year |
| **Monthly consumption** | ≈ 833 kWh/month |
| **Daily consumption** | ≈ 27.7 kWh/day |

> **Why this range?**  
> • **Climate:** Homes in colder climates may use more heating, while hotter climates may use more cooling.  
> • **Insulation & windows:** Better insulation reduces heating/cooling load.  
> • **Appliances & electronics:** High‑efficiency appliances lower usage; many devices on standby add up.  
> • **Occupancy & habits:** More occupants or frequent use of high‑power devices (e.g., ovens, HVAC) increase demand.

### How to Refine the Estimate

1. **Check past utility bills** – Look at your last 12 months of electric usage (in kWh).  
2. **Use a home energy calculator** – Many utilities offer online tools where you input square footage, climate zone, and appliance list.  
3. **Consider local weather patterns** – If you live in a very hot or cold area, adjust upward or downward by 10–20%.  

If you’d like a more precise calculation tailored to your specific situation (e.g., exact square footage, average sunlight hours if you’re considering solar, or your current energy efficiency rating), let me know and I can run a quick estimate for you!
